chunks: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan narrated from Amr ibn Sa'id from Musaddiq ibn Sadah from 'Ammar al-Sabati who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who says, 'Fasting is incumbent upon me for a month, or more than that, or less,' and a matter arises that requires him to travel. Should he fast while traveling? He said: 'When he travels, he should break the fast, because fasting is not permissible for him during travel, whether it is obligatory or not, and fasting during travel is an act of disobedience.'

From 'Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: I asked him about a man who has days remaining from the month of Ramadan, how should he make them up? He said: 'If he has two days, he should break the fast for one day between them; and if he has five days, he should break the fast for two days between them; and if he has a month, he should break the fast for days between them. And he is not permitted to fast more than eight days consecutively. If he has eight days or ten days, he should break the fast for one day between them.'
ai.seo_question: How should a Muslim make up missed Ramadan fasts if they have a vow to fast for a specific number of days?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the practical application of fasting laws during travel and the specific methodology for making up missed Ramadan days (qada). It establishes that fasting while traveling is considered an act of disobedience (ma'siyah), whether the fast is obligatory or voluntary, and prescribes a structured pattern of alternating fasting and non-fasting days to prevent excessive continuous fasting, capped at eight consecutive days. This ruling highlights the Shia emphasis on balancing religious devotion with ease and avoiding hardship in ritual observance.
